   Cold Storage removes NZ brand Homegrown apple juice after HK flags high toxin levels

 Set as preferred source Listen Summarise 中文 Cold Storage removed Homegrown 100% Pure NZ Apple Juice after Hong Kong found patulin at 79 micrograms per kilogram, above the legal limit of 50 mcg per kg.
 Singapore’s SFA said it told the importer to stop sales and keep the affected batch off shelves to protect food safety.

 AI generated
 SINGAPORE – Supermarket chain Cold Storage has removed New Zealand brand Homegrown’s apple juice from its shelves after the Hong Kong authorities flagged excessive toxin levels in a batch of the drink.
 In response to media queries on Nov 21, the Singapore Food Agency (SFA) said it was notified that the Hong Kong authorities had found high levels of the mycotoxin patulin, exceeding the legal limit, in samples of Homegrown 100% Pure NZ Apple Juice.
 The affected batch consists of one-litre bottles with a best-before date of Feb 11, 2027, imported from The Homegrown Juice Company.
 According to a Nov 17 press statement from Hong Kong’s Centre for Food Safety, a sample collected from a wholesale market in Sai Ying Pun contained patulin at 79 micrograms per kilogram, exceeding the legal limit of 50mcg per kilogram.
 The SFA engaged the importer, Cold Storage , which voluntarily removed the affected batch from sale.
 The agency also issued a direction to bar the affected products from being sold in Singapore, and will continue monitoring the situation to ensure food safety.
 Patulin is a heat-stable toxin produced by moulds and is mainly found in rotting apples and apple products, the SFA said, adding that it can survive processing .
 Consuming excessive amounts of patulin can cause acute symptoms such as nausea, vomiting and gastrointestinal disturbances.
 Under Singapore’s Sale of Food Act, food products that fail to meet safety requirements cannot be sold.
 As a precaution, consumers who have bought the affected product should not drink it. Those who have consumed the product and have health concerns should seek medical advice, the SFA advised.
 Consumers with inquiries may contact their point of purchase, the agency added.
 The Straits Times has contacted Cold Storage and FairPrice , which also lists the apple juice on its website, for more information.
